description: Product registry: which Products the Marketing Engineer serves, their gates, and the read-only locations of each Product's repository and Go-To-Market Package. It records where strategy lives, never the strategy itself.
path_resolution: A local path starting with ~/ resolves against the home directory of the account running the Marketing Engineer. On a machine with a different layout, set the environment variable named in a location's env field to an absolute path; it replaces that location's default. Paths inside Mandu are relative to the resolved Mandu checkout. The sandbox reads every Product repository, and of Mandu only each Product's package paths (go_to_market_package: its path, launch_checklist, and sources) and nothing else in that checkout; a Product's Waitlist view and its footage folders are read by the launcher alone.

mandu.holds: Each Product's Go-To-Market Package and nothing else gr0wthlab reads: the Founder's decisions and records are in this repository's ledger/founder/, written by `src/bin/gr0wthlab sitting` (docs/adr/0002-the-founder-decides-in-gr0wthlab.md). What Mandu may read from gr0wthlab: docs/mandu-exchange.md.

go_to_market_package.sources_note: The package sources each run snapshots, from the PRD's list; a path ending in / covers every file under it, or only the files whose names start with files_starting_with. Every source also feeds the package review, so a failed one makes that review incomplete as well as the outputs it names.

post_drafts.note: Which package file plays each part in the post-Draft checks (US-ME08); each is one of the sources above, so every run snapshots it. The competitors are the ones the research names in its files that start with competitor. The filming plan (US-ME09) reads its shot lists from the same calendar, angles, and pairs files.

weekly_read.note: read_the_results is the package file that holds the binding rules for reading results (US-ME12), which the Weekly Read session applies; the launcher reads it only for the floor's own figure, and for whether it already says the floor counts views. It is one of the sources above, and the rules are never restated here. The calendar, the Angle bank, and the pairs the read covers are post_drafts' files. creative_log is the package's own record of each Angle's status, where the calendar's kill rule marks a killed Angle: the launcher reads it only in a run whose approved Weekly Read kill or change owes its package-change proposal, to make that proposal's exact edit, a change's adding the new Angle's record (src/gr0wthlab/weekly_changes.py). It is not one of the sources above, so no run snapshots it and the package review does not review it; it lies under the package path, which the sandbox reads.

listening.note: The package file that defines the customer the Product is built for, which the Marketing Engineer reads to score each Listening quote's Fit (US-ME13); it is one of the sources above, and the definition is never restated here. The competitors whose App Store reviews are read are post_drafts.competitors, each by the store page its own section of the research cites. The places Listening reads are in config/sources.json.

outreach.note: The package file that names the personal-network ask and the creators worth writing to (US-ME14); one of the sources above covers it. A run drafts a message only for a creator in config/run.json that this file still names.

footage.note: The agreed place where the Founder drops raw footage, which the Founder named on 2026-10-11: RepToday's own folder in Mandu, holding one window-<n>/ footage folder per 14-day window beside the package in gtm/, each file named for its shot of the filming plan (docs/operations.md has the naming). It changes only through a reviewed change, and is never inferred; it is written from the home folder, so it does not move with GR0WTHLAB_MANDU_DIR, and a machine that overrides that sets the env named here too. The launcher only ever reads the footage folders, to fingerprint and measure each file and to cut finished assets from it; nothing in gr0wthlab writes, renames, or deletes anything there. The sandboxed agent reads nothing in a footage folder: of Mandu the permission profile grants only the package paths above, and the launcher refuses to start when a grant covers the footage place or lies in one of its footage folders, or when a place outside Mandu holds anything the sandbox reads (keep_footage_unread in src/gr0wthlab/boundary.py); the preflight then shows the sandbox refused a listing of each footage folder before each session's agent starts.

filming.note: Filming (US-ME09). Which assets need the Founder or a real device, their shot lists, and their sittings come from the kit in Mandu every run. Finished assets go to ledger/assets/, outside git; the canvas they are finished at is in config/platforms.json.

view.note: The anonymous Waitlist view RepToday's Waitlist build produces, in the format its Dispatch request specifies. Only the launcher reads it, never the sandboxed agent, so it must lie outside this repository and every location above; the launcher refuses to start otherwise. null until the build lands (US-ME05), when a reviewed change sets its path.

waitlist.note: How each run counts the view (US-ME06): the Source tags and Fit answers the Dispatch request defines, unknown for a sign-up with no tag or no answer; good Fit is the 'used to exercise and lost the routine' answer unless the Founder approves another definition, which is one reviewed edit to good_fit; progress is good-Fit opt-ins toward the Beta Cohort bar of about 50.

beta_recruiting.note: Beta Cohort recruiting (US-ME15), which does nothing until the Founder records an approved Beta Build on the sitting page (ledger/founder/beta-builds/, docs/mandu-exchange.md). k8 is the folder of the thesis and its K8 rubric, which every invitation cites; brand_rules is the brand lint's one rule source. A recruiting Draft may cite a line of any package source above that beta-recruiting needs, and of no other file. cohort is the Beta Cohort's size, 20 to 50 people: recruiting goes on until the Founder reports that it reached the maximum or records a stop, and a pool that cannot reach the minimum is reported with its gap. The size of a batch is the Founder's call in config/run.json.

products.name: Immerse
products.go_to_market_package_note: Immerse has no Go-To-Market Package yet. Its Listening Evidence feeds Immerse's naming decision and a future package in Mandu through package-change proposals.
